top.title: Best performers from 49ers' shootout win vs. Cowboys
top.description: The San Francisco 49ers traveled south to take on the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Sunday for a battle between non-division NFC rivals, and Kyle Shanahan's team earned a 46-40 win, moving to 8-1 on the year. San Francisco's offense played very well, while the defense left a lot to be desired, but it was enough to drop the Cowboys to 4-6. As we continue to comb through this victory, let's take a look at some of San Francisco's top performers from this Week 10 matchup. QB Brock Purdy Purdy played an incredible game despite being under constant pressure and taking five sacks. He completed 78.6% of his passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns while rushing for another 21 yards on two scrambles. This looked like the performance of a potential MVP. RB Christian McCaffrey Sunday was one of the best games of McCaffrey's career. He rushed for 62 yards and a touchdown on 4.8 yards per attempt, but he was even more effective as a pass catcher, hauling in all four of his targets for 161 yards and two touchdowns. Not being forced to be the bell cow this year has really helped him this year. RB Kaelon Black Spelling McCaffrey a lot this year, Black has played really well in his rookie year. Against the Cowboys, he ran for 53 yards and a touchdown on 4.8 yards per attempt. His 25-yard score was incredible, as he ran over two defenders on his way to the end zone. Black also caught two passes for 13 yards. WR Deebo Samuel Samuel made his return to the field this week after missing time due to an injury. He caught three passes for 31 yards, including an 11-yard touchdown. He also carried the ball three times for 78 yards, including a 70-yard score on a reverse. Samuel brings a different dimension to this offseason when he's healthy. top.title: Are 49ers due for a reality check? Red flags emerged in wild win over Cowboys
top.description: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy, bottom, is sacked by Dallas Cowboys defensive tackle LT Overton during the first half on Sunday in Arlington, Texas. (Tony Gutierrez/Associated Press) The San Francisco 49ers second travelogue trip of the season got off to an exciting start on Sunday, surviving a wild - and somewhat alarming - shootout with the Dallas Cowboys, 46-40. Now they head from the plains of Texas to the Rocky Mountains and then take a hard left to go south of the border to Mexico City, during their second lengthy, multi-country trip. The good news is the 49ers are tied for a league best 8-1. The better news - for the coaches - is that, during this long week away from home, the 49ers have plenty to keep them occupied. Like tightening up that problematic defense. Improving the pass rush. And keeping Brock Purdy upright. Twelve days after Democrats turned Texas blue, 49ers fans turned Dallas red, taking over AT&T Stadium and making Jerry Jones' palace sound like their home stadium. For the fans' next trick, they'll try to turn Mexico red. "Our fans are awesome," head coach Kyle Shanahan said. "Wish I could give them all game balls." The 49ers have cruised to an 8-1 record, and the most impressive part of the first half of the season has been vanquishing their most heated rivals away from their home stadium: the Rams in Australia, the Seahawks in Seattle and, on Sunday, the Cowboys, in Arlington, Texas. But the upcoming second half of the season holds some potential concerns. And Sunday's split personality game underscored those worries. "It was sort of a weird game," Purdy said. While the 49ers offense looked like the most elite on the planet on Sunday, racking up 584 yards, the 49ers defense couldn't say the same thing. The 49ers swamped the Cowboys from the end of the second quarter until early in the fourth quarter, outscoring Dallas 28-3 in that stretch. But then the 49ers found themselves in an uncomfortably tight situation, giving up three Dallas touchdowns in the final 9:08 of the game and having to survive an onside kick, their own fumble (that they recovered), a three-and-out and a Dallas attempt at a Cal Bears-style lateral-fest comeback. "Anytime you get 40 dropped on you, you're going to be upset," said linebacker Fred Warner . "You've got to look at the tape and see why that was the case." There will be a lot of tape to watch in the coming week, while getting acclimated to altitude in Colorado Springs. Though the first half of the season has gone almost perfectly, there is still a long road ahead. Next week, in Estadio Azteca, the 49ers will face Minnesota, a team that - unlike the Cowboys - will present a ferocious defense. And, with the addition of Kirk Cousins, a team that suddenly looks like a true Super Bowl contender. LOS ANGELES -- It was a fun afternoon for the No. 21 USC Trojans on Sunday at the Galen Center. Trouncing the Arkansas-Pine Bluff Golden Lions 122-46, the squad improved to 4-0 on the season to open up a three-game homestand. The 76-point victory marked the largest margin of victory in program history. The victory also marks the seventh time in head coach Eric Musselman's career that his teams have started the season with four consecutive wins. Sunday showcased a wire-to-wire, well-rounded effort led by a dominant performance from forward Adonis Ratliff. "I feel like today it was easy to show off my playmaking," Ratliff said. "I feel like I'm a pretty good passer. I don't get to show it much, but I feel like I was able to do that today." It was an Adonis avalanche from the beginning, as the freshman got the Trojans out to an 8-0 advantage all by himself. He put back a missed attempt from his brother Darius before drilling back-to-back triples and forcing an early timeout from the Golden Lions. Adonis continued to fill up the stat sheet in more ways than one, making his presence felt just as strongly on the defensive end of the floor. By the end of the afternoon, he compiled 17 points to go along with eight rebounds, five assists and four blocks. top.title: Joe Flacco replaces Joe Burrow in 4th quarter of Bengals-Steelers rout
top.description: Cincinnati Bengals backup quarterback Joe Flacco entered in the fourth quarter of the team's NFL Week 10 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football , as the Bengals sat starter Joe Burrow with a 38-18 lead. Burrow left the game having completed 35-of-44 for 409 passing yards with four touchdowns. He had 302 passing yards in the first half . When Flacco started for the Bengals in 2025 against Aaron Rodgers, ESPN Research reported that it was the second time in NFL history that two quarterbacks at least 40 years old face off in a regular-season or postseason game. The Steelers' Cam Heyward dubbed it the "Icy Hot" Bowl . Rodgers is the only active NFL quarterback older than Flacco. Rodgers' announcement in May that he'll retire after the 2026 season means the Bengals may not face the future Pro Football Hall of Famer again. Flacco got to enter the team's NFL Week 7 rout of the Ravens in Baltimore during the fourth quarter and finish the game against his former team, but he did not attempt a pass. Flacco entered Week 7 having appeared in one game for the Bengals this season but without attempting a pass. Flacco told Burrow he thought Burrow's first touchdown pass to Ja'Marr Chase against the Houston Texans was "uncatchable." Rodgers' announcement in May that he'll retire after the 2026 season means the Bengals may not face the future Pro Football Hall of Famer again. Flacco, who turned 41 in January, played in nine games last season for the Bengals , making six starts after Burrow suffered a turf toe injury during a Week 2 win against Jacksonville . Flacco completed 158 of 254 pass attempts for 1,664 yards with 13 touchdowns. In November 2025, Flacco played with a sprained AC joint in his throwing shoulder during a 47-42 loss to the Chicago Bears . (Photo by Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) Getty Several players made big plays for the Kansas City Chiefs during their 35-13 victory over the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday. It started with quarterback Patrick Mahomes, who threw for 348 yards and five touchdowns. He hit four different pass catchers in the endzone — including running back Emmett Johnson twice, as well as wide receivers Josh Downs, Cyrus Allen, and Andrew Armstrong. Kansas City Chiefs WR Xavier Worthy Facing Backlash for Effort Issues vs. Falcons One playmaker who did not contribute to beating Atlanta was third-year man Xavier Worthy. Despite leading all Chiefs receivers in snaps played with 56, he failed to catch a single pass on the day. Late during the second quarter, Worthy had the ball in his hands for what initially appeared to be a catch, but he dropped it as he fell to the ground. Fast forward to midway through the fourth quarter, the Falcons scored their first touchdown to make the score 28-10. They then executed an onside kick and recovered it. The ball bounced over Worthy’s head, and he did not make much of an attempt to make a play on the ball. Ben Solak and JP Acosta are a couple of notable analysts who called Worthy out. top.description: Cincinnati Bengals linebacker Oren Burks was injured during the second half of the NFL Week 10 game between the Bengals and Pittsburgh at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football. The Bengals declared Burks out with a groin injury during the fourth quarter. Burks is in his ninth NFL season, second with the Bengals. He played in all 17 games for Cincinnati in his first season with the team. In March 2025, the Bengals gave Burks, then an unrestricted free agent, a two-year, $5 million deal. Burks played in 17 games in 2024 for the Philadelphia Eagles, making two starts. During the playoffs, Burks replaced the injured Nakobe Dean for Philly, and had 25 tackles, 3 tackles for loss, one sack and two QB hits. Burks played in 59 games over four NFL seasons with the Green Bay Packers to start his career. He played in 32 games over two seasons with the San Francisco 49ers, and became a free agent in March 2024. He played in three postseason games in each of his seasons with the Niners. top.description: Las Vegas Raiders QB Fernando Mendoza. Getty It wasn’t the magical debut start that Fernando Mendoza and the Las Vegas Raiders were likely hoping for. The team has held off on playing the No. 1 pick for nine games, but that changed in Week 10 against the Seattle Seahawks. At first, it looked like the Raiders might make it a competitive game. The offense scored a touchdown on the opening drive, and Mendoza was distributing the ball all around. However, star tight end Brock Bowers went down with an ankle injury in the first half. He tried to play through the pain, but the Raiders made the decision to rule him out at the start of the second half. It was clear that set the offense back. Mendoza had a much harder time finding open receivers. The Raiders already can’t run the ball, so not having Bowers made things even harder. Mendoza loves Bowers, but he wasn’t ready to make excuses for the loss. “Brock’s a fantastic player. I mean, he’s a special human being on and off the field,” Mendoza told reporters after the game. “However, coach Kubiak always preaches everybody doing their jobs. So the next guy up, I have as much confidence in, and so I just need to get the ball to the right players on time and efficiently and accurately.” No Update on Bowers Injury There are few skill players in the NFL as important to a team as Bowers is to the Raiders. He’s easily their best offensive player and seems to be the only one who is consistently making plays. The Raiders survived two games without him at the start of the season, but they’re going to have almost no chance against the Denver Broncos in Week 11 if he can’t play. top.description: Cincinnati Bengals receiver Ja'Marr Chase had more than 200 receiving yards in a game for the fourth time in his NFL career during the team's NFL Week 10 showdown with the Pittsburgh Steelers on NBC's Sunday Night Football at Paycor Stadium. Chase eclipsed the 200-yard mark on a 42-yard catch from quarterback Joe Burrow during the fourth quarter. It was his 11th catch of the game, for 230 receiving yards. In 2022, Chase's 266 yards were the most in a game by a rookie in NFL history. Chase had 264 receiving yards against Baltimore in 2024 and 201 yards against the Ravens in 2021. Chase told reporters during the week that he loves primetime games . After the Bengals' Week 9 win against Atlanta at Bernabéu Stadium in Madrid, Spain, Chase and quarterback Joe Burrow exchanged jerseys with Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois. Burrow was asked by NFL Network sideline reporter Molly McGrath about Chase's impact against Atlanta . "An intense impact, very intense," Burrow said. "He was unbelievable today. (I) just try to keep finding ways to get him the ball. He's gonna keep doing his thing. We had a lot of one-high defenses today. And we've got to make them pay when we get that. And he certainly did." Chase had the biggest first half of his NFL career in terms of receiving yardage, with 142 yards and a touchdown during the first half in Madrid. Chase and Tee Higgins celebrated Chase's first-quarter TD with a bullfighting nod . Chase was seen screaming on the Bengals' sideline just after teammate Mike Gesicki caught a go-ahead touchdown pass from Burrow with 7:13 left in regulation during the team's NFL Week 8 overtime win against Tennessee. top.title: Falcons’ Kevin Stefanski takes full responsibility for offense’s dud vs. Chiefs
top.description: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Falcons’ Kevin Stefanski takes full responsibility for offense’s dud vs. Chiefs appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Atlanta Falcons offense laid a proverbial egg against the Kansas City Chiefs on Week 10. They were thumped 35-13 and were down 28-3 at one point in the fourth quarter. It got so bad that the Falcons’ own fans started to boo them. Falcons quarterback Michael Penix Jr. finished 23 of 43 with 286 yards, no touchdowns, and one interception. When a reported asked Kevin Stefanski postgame how much of the responsibility for the offense’s poor performance fell on Penix Jr., the Falcons head coach took the fall for his QB . “The responsibility falls on me, all of this falls on me. I’ll take responsibility for everything that goes on in this football team. We all have to be better. That’s the truth. We will all learn from it. We’re not going to hid from it. We’re going to own it and then make corrections,” Stefanski said. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) After a promising start to the season headlined by high-scoring wins over the Packers and Saints, the Falcons offense has fallen flat in recent weeks. They’ve scored just 30 total points over their last three games (all losses), including a goose egg in their 16-0 defeat to the Tampa Bay Buccaneers. Penix Jr. has thrown just one touchdown pass during those three games. And to make matters worse, his top receiver Drake London suffered a suspected concussion against the Chiefs and could potentially miss time. But as Stefanski emphatically reminded everyone, the responsibility is on him to get the Falcons offense firing once again. He will have time to think things through during their bye next week. After that, the Falcons will come back-to-back tough tests against the Minnesota Vikings and Detroit Lions. nigeria.title: JAN advances children’s digital safety, literacy through ‘Be Internet Awesome’ program
nigeria.description: As digital technology increasingly shapes how children learn, communicate, and interact with the world, equipping them to navigate the internet safely and responsibly has become more important than ever. In response, Junior Achievement Nigeria (JAN), with support from Google.org, is equipping 57,000 pupils aged 7 to 13 across 25 states of the Federation with essential digital literacy and online safety skills through its Be Internet Awesome (BIA) program. Be Internet Awesome is designed to help children become confident and responsible digital citizens by equipping them with the knowledge to recognise online risks, protect their personal information, think critically about what they encounter online and make informed decisions in digital spaces. Through engaging, age-appropriate learning experiences, participants explore key aspects of digital citizenship, including protecting personal information, identifying misinformation, recognising potential online threats, practising kindness online and knowing how to respond to uncomfortable or unsafe digital experiences. Beyond teaching children how to use digital tools, the program encourages them to understand the consequences of their online actions and develop positive digital habits. Speaking on the program’s implementation, Moradeke Ayokanmbi, Program Officer, Be Internet Awesome, Junior Achievement Nigeria, said: “Children are engaging with the digital world at increasingly younger ages, making it important that they understand not just how to use the internet, but how to navigate it safely. “Through Be Internet Awesome, we are creating opportunities for participants to learn practical digital safety skills, think critically about what they encounter online and understand the importance of responsible digital behaviour. “We are also encouraging parents and teachers to become active partners in this journey because keeping children safe online is a shared responsibility.” Recognising that children’s online experiences are shaped by the environments and people around them, the program also places emphasis on engaging the adults responsible for their care and development. Teachers, parents and caregivers are encouraged to reinforce the lessons children learn and support them in building safer, more responsible online habits. nigeria.title: Diabetes: CAPPA urges FG, states to impose 20% sugary drinks tax, reform food policies
nigeria.description: By Chioma Obinna On this day World Diabetes Day, the Corporate Accountability and Public Participation Africa (CAPPA) on Saturday called on the Federal Government and state governments to urgently reform Nigeria’s food policies, impose a minimum 20 per cent tax on sugar-sweetened beverages and tighten regulations on unhealthy food products to curb the rising burden of diabetes. The organisation warned that efforts to tackle the disease would yield limited results if government focused on screening and treatment while allowing aggressive marketing, widespread availability and affordability of ultra-processed foods and sugary drinks to continue unchecked. Making the call in a message to mark the 2026 World Diabetes Day, marked November 14, with the theme, “Early Action on Diabetes”, CAPPA said Nigeria faced an escalating diabetes crisis that required decisive government intervention beyond public awareness and individual lifestyle changes. According to the organisation, Nigeria has the highest number of adults aged 20 to 79 living with diabetes in Africa, while nearly three in four adults with diabetes across the continent remain undiagnosed. It warned that delayed diagnosis exposes millions of Nigerians to potentially life-threatening complications, including kidney failure, blindness, stroke and amputations. CAPPA also raised the alarm over the financial burden of diet-related non-communicable diseases, citing an estimated N1.92 trillion annual out-of-pocket expenditure by Nigerian households on their treatment. Executive Director of CAPPA, Akinbode Oluwafemi, said diabetes prevention should not be reduced to individual discipline when commercial interests and unhealthy food environments increasingly shape people’s dietary choices. He said: “We cannot keep telling Nigerians to eat healthily while allowing unhealthy food and beverages to dominate our markets, schools, advertisements and public spaces. “Early action on diabetes must begin with enacting and implementing strong regulatory policies that make healthy choices possible, affordable and accessible, not simply with advising people to change their dietary behaviour.” The organisation cited its 2025 report, Junk On Our Plates, which documented aggressive marketing of ultra-processed foods and beverages high in sugar and sodium across seven Nigerian states. It said the report exposed the targeting of children, young people and low-income communities through advertising, celebrity endorsements, misleading nutrition labels and cultural imagery designed to promote unhealthy products. To reverse the trend, CAPPA outlined five major policy interventions, beginning with the conclusion and enforcement of the proposed Sugar-Sweetened Beverage (SSB) tax. It urged the House of Representatives and the Federal Executive to complete legislative action following the Senate’s passage of the tax review bill earlier this year. The organisation advocated an inflation-adjusted excise tax of at least 20 per cent

nigeria.title: 2027: Soludo urges politicians to keep off places of worship
nigeria.description: Gov. Chukwuma Soludo of Anambra has urged politicians to keep politics away from places of worship, saying religious institutions should remain centres of spiritual growth and unity. Soludo made the call during a visit to the Mountain of Holy Ghost Intervention Deliverance Ministry Inc., Onitsha, to celebrate its 30th anniversary. The ministry was founded by Prophet Chukwuemeka Ohanaemere, popularly known as Odumeje. He said: “Politicians, keep off places of worship! I do not do politics in the house of God. “I deliberately avoided church campaigns for six months before the last governorship election in Anambra. “My visit to religious institutions is usually motivated by my commitment to ecumenism and responsibility as the father of all in the state”. The governor described the anniversary as a significant milestone, noting that it marked maturity, preparation and a new phase in the ministry’s growth. He recalled that his first encounter with the ministry was during the demolition of part of its structure by the state government to facilitate the dredging of the Sakamori drainage channel. Soludo commended Odumeje for his contributions to charity and efforts towards societal development. He also acknowledged the cleric’s support for the state’s campaign against criminal idolatry and activities of illegal traditional spiritual practitioners. According to him, the advocacy, alongside the Anambra Homeland Security Law, has contributed to making the state safer. Responding, Odumeje pledged continued partnership with the state government to drive progress and development. nigeria.title: Igbokoda Crash: NAF recovers black box, holds memorial November 26
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The Nigerian Air Force (NAF) has confirmed the recovery of the Cockpit Voice Recorder (CVR) from the site of the October 5 aircraft crash at Igbokoda, Ondo State, announcing plans to hold a memorial service and wreath-laying ceremony for the victims on November 26. The ceremony will take place at the National Military Cemetery, Abuja, in honour of the personnel and other victims who lost their lives in the NAF 931 aircraft accident. NAF Director of Public Relations and Information, Air Commodore Ehimen Ejodame, disclosed this in a statement on Sunday, saying the event would provide an opportunity for bereaved families, colleagues, friends and members of the Air Force community to pay their last respects. He said the ceremony would also serve as a formal expression of the Service’s respect and remembrance for those who died in the incident. On the recovery of the aircraft’s black box, Ejodame said the CVR, alongside other aircraft fragments and relevant evidence, had been retrieved from the crash site. He explained that data recovered from the voice recorder was being analysed and was expected to contribute significantly to the ongoing investigation into the circumstances surrounding the accident. According to him, the investigation is progressing in collaboration with the Nigerian Safety Investigation Bureau (NSIB) and the Nigerian Civil Aviation Authority (NCAA). The Air Force reiterated its commitment to ensuring that the investigation was conducted in accordance with the highest standards of professionalism, transparency, accountability and responsibility, while supporting the independent technical processes required to establish the cause of the crash. Ejodame further disclosed that recovery operations had yielded several human remains and aircraft fragments, while the identification process for the recovered remains was ongoing. He said the operation had been particularly challenging because of the swampy nature of the terrain and the depth to which some of the aircraft wreckage had penetrated the ground. The NAF spokesman added that the Service was engaging relevant agencies to address environmental concerns arising from the recovery exercise and ensure appropriate remediation after its completion. He said the Air Force recognised the grief of the bereaved families and remained committed to providing them with sustained support throughout the difficult period. The Service also appreciated the cooperation of relevant agencies, host communities and other stakeholders who had continued to support the recovery and investigation efforts. The NAF assured the public of its commitment to a thorough investigation, responsible environmental management and the dignified remembrance of all those who lost their lives. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Falls 14% in a Week to $65,000 as Weekend Selling Breaks Friday’s Low Bitcoin price crashed about 14% over the past week and was trading near $65,200 on Saturday morning after sliding to about $65,000, according to Bitcoin Magazine Pro data. The move broke below Friday’s low of about $67,555 and marked the weakest level since mid-August, as weekend trading extended a selloff that has followed a stronger dollar and a fully priced December Federal Reserve rate hike. A week ago, on Nov. 7, bitcoin was trading near $75,750. The decline steepened after Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on Thursday, a shake-up that caused AI stocks to sell off which could potentially be responsible for sending bitcoin below $72,000. It slipped toward $71,000 by Thursday evening, then crashed to about $67,555 around midnight Eastern on Friday, its lowest level since August, before recovering toward $69,800 in the morning. A brief pop above $70,000 after the producer-price report faded, and the bitcoin price spent Friday afternoon pinned below $70,000, near $68,900. Selling resumed Friday evening and carried into the mid-$66,000s. Bitcoin briefly steadied overnight near $67,000, then sold off again after 8 a.m. ET Saturday, reaching that $65,500 low in the 10 a.m. hour and taking out Friday’s trough. A stronger dollar and higher yields still weigh on the bitcoin price The Labor Department said Friday that the Producer Price Index for final demand rose 0.3% in October, short of the 0.4% increase economists had expected. On an unadjusted basis, the index was up 6.5% from a year earlier, the largest 12-month rise since November 2022. The slightly cooler monthly figure lifted bitcoin above $70,000 for only minutes. Bond traders were unconvinced. The 10-year Treasury yield climbed as high as 5.17% on Friday, a four-week high, and closed at 5.15%. The U.S. dollar index held at a 19-month high, its strongest level since April 2025. Boston Fed President Susan Collins said Friday that “soon, some additional tightening of Fed monetary policy may be appropriate,” and San Francisco Fed President Mary Daly said policymakers will, “in all likelihood, raise interest rates.” Higher rates raise the cost of holding an asset that pays no interest, and a stronger dollar has weighed on the bitcoin price for much of November. entertainment.title: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar Makes History as First Female Vice-Chancellor of UNIJOS
entertainment.description: Professor Patricia Mamko Lar, appointed as the 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor and first female Vice-Chancellor of the University of Jos. The University of Jos (UNIJOS) has officially appointed Professor Patricia Mamko Lar as its 11th substantive Vice-Chancellor, making her the first woman to occupy the position since the institution was established in 1971. Announced on Thursday, 12 November 2026 by the university’s Pro-Chancellor and Chairman of Council, Senator Grace Folashade Bent , during a special meeting of the 15th Governing Council, the historic appointment sees Professor Lar succeed Professor Tanko Ishaya as she takes the helm of the Plateau State institution. Born in Langtang, Plateau State, Professor Lar is a distinguished Professor of Medical Microbiology whose career has been deeply woven into the fabric of UNIJOS for nearly four decades. After earning her Bachelor of Science degree in Microbiology from Ahmadu Bello University, Zaria in 1986, she joined the University of Jos in 1987 as a Graduate Assistant in the Department of Medical Microbiology. She later went on to earn her Master’s degree in Medical Microbiology in 1989 and her PhD in Medical Parasitology in 1998 from the University of Lagos, followed by postdoctoral training at the Institute of Human Virology, University of Maryland in the United States under the NIH-Fogarty Fellowship Programme. Rising steadily through the academic ranks, she became an Associate Professor in 2012 before attaining full professorship in October 2015. Over the years, she has built an impressive body of work with more than 40 scholarly publications focusing on infectious diseases, including HIV/AIDS, malaria, antimicrobial resistance, and phytomedicine. Beyond the lecture hall and laboratory, Professor Lar has also served in key administrative roles at UNIJOS—including Head of the Department of Microbiology and Director of Linkages and Collaborations—and previously served a six-month tenure as Acting Vice-Chancellor of Yakubu Gowon University (formerly the University of Abuja) following her appointment by President Bola Tinubu in February 2025. Alongside her academic and leadership credentials, Professor Lar is a recognised advocate for women’s empowerment, having received the He4She Certificate of Award for Women Empowerment Activism in 2019. As she begins her five-year single term as UNIJOS’s first female substantive Vice-Chancellor after 55 years, she brings nearly four decades of institutional experience to the university’s top seat. entertainment.title: Ramla Ali Wins IBF and WBO Titles to Become Somalia’s First Boxing World Champion
entertainment.description: Unified world champion Ramla Ali poses in the ring with her WBO and IBF super-bantamweight belts and her coaching team in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram British-Somali boxer and fashion model Ramla Ali is officially a unified world champion! On 8 November 2026 at the College Park Center in Arlington, Texas, the 37-year-old athlete captured the vacant IBF and WBO super-bantamweight world titles after securing a split-decision victory over American contender Mikiah Kreps . During the ten-round bout, Ali dropped Kreps with a sharp right hand in the third round—the sole knockdown of the night—before two judges scored the contest 97–92 and 96–93 in her favour, against one scorecard of 98–91 for Kreps. With this triumph, Ali became Somalia’s first-ever professional boxing world champion and a unified titleholder in one unforgettable night. Born in Mogadishu, Somalia, she fled the civil war as a child with her family and grew up in East London, initially taking up boxing in secret as a teenager before turning it into a life-changing calling. Ramla Ali makes her ring walk behind the Somali and British flags ahead of her super-bantamweight world title fight in Arlington, Texas. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Her remarkable journey from refugee to Olympic athlete and champion is also the subject of the biographical feature film In the Shadows. Directed by Anthony Wonke , the film premiered at the 70th BFI London Film Festival on 9 October 2026 before opening in UK and Irish cinemas on 30 October—just over a week before she lifted her world title belts in Texas. BAFTA-winning Top Boy actress Jasmine Jobson stars as Ali alongside Peaky Blinders actor Finn Cole as her husband and former coach, Richard Moore , with both Ali and Moore serving as executive producers on the project. This championship milestone builds on a string of barrier-breaking firsts across sports, cinema, and fashion. Long before her title win in Arlington, Ali made history as the first Muslim woman to win an English amateur boxing title, the first boxer to win an international gold medal while representing Somalia, and the first boxer to represent Somalia on the Olympic stage when she competed in the women’s featherweight division at the Tokyo 2020 Summer Olympics. Ramla Ali celebrates in the ring as the referee raises her hand following her split-decision victory over Mikiah Kreps on 8 November 2026. Photo Credit: Yahya Ali/Instagram Away from the ring, she has carved out an equally notable space in global luxury fashion. Ali has graced the covers of British Vogue, Elle UK, Harper’s Bazaar Arabia, and Grazia UK, served as a brand ambassador for Cartier and Dior, and made history as the first boxer to wear custom ring attire created by major fashion houses—including bespoke fight kits designed by Dior, Off-White, Versace, Alexander McQueen, and Burberry featuring the panther emblem from Somalia’s coat of arms. entertainment.title: Ayobami Esther Akinnagbe: Organisational Mistakes Start-up Founders Should Avoid
entertainment.description: Two women engaged in a professional meeting, discussing business in a modern office setting. Image by RDNE Stock project for Pexels . There is a lot that goes into establishing a successful business. It requires developing the business idea, securing clients, building a customer base and eventually bringing people on board. Starting a business and watching it grow can be an exciting experience. However, one thing many start-up founders overlook is the importance of having the right organisational structure in place. It is one thing to have a great business idea and attract talented employees, but it is another thing to create an environment where everyone understands their responsibilities, knows who they report to and can work effectively towards achieving the company’s objectives. I once worked with a client who needed a new set of employees for a business establishment that was reopening after a period of restructuring. As part of the recruitment process, the first thing I ensured was that a manager was hired before proceeding to fill the remaining vacancies. The idea was simple. The manager would oversee the day-to-day running of the establishment, ensure that company policies were implemented and periodically train employees based on the requirements of their respective roles. During the recruitment process, I clearly communicated each employee’s responsibilities and the person they would be reporting to. These details were also stated in their respective offer letters, so everyone understood their roles and the management structure they were expected to work within. However, there was a challenge. Before the manager was hired, an accountant who was personally known to both co-founders had also been in charge of the previous employees. Following the restructuring, the founders had communicated their desire for a new operational arrangement, and this was clearly reflected in the recruitment brief. Although the new employees understood that they were expected to report to the newly hired manager, the existing employees still had their loyalty to the accountant, who had previously been in charge. The challenge was that the new management structure had not been properly implemented within the organisation. Consequently, the manager was expected to take charge of the establishment without the necessary authority and cooperation from everyone involved. This created unnecessary friction, and I found myself having to mediate whenever issues arose, even though the service I had been engaged to provide was recruitment. I eventually had a lengthy conversation with one of the founders, explaining that communicating reporting lines and responsibilities during recruitment was only one part of the process. entertainment.title: Uwaezu Kanu: Why Motherhood Feels Different for Women in Their 40s Today
entertainment.description: “Oh my God, Uwaezu! You need to hear the latest gist!” My younger sister buzzed with excitement. Though we had been living in different countries for a couple of years, we still made time to talk every single week. Unfortunately, when she called, I couldn’t talk on the phone as I had been ambushed by my kids, who were brandishing their homework and threatening to cry if I didn’t help them. As a mom herself, she immediately understood why I couldn’t continue with the conversation. I quickly made my excuses, and we laughed and hung up, promising to catch up at a more convenient time. However, that exchange got me thinking about how most millennial women have a radically different marriage and motherhood timeline from our mothers. You see, when my mother was in her early 40s, my siblings and I were in university, so she had a lot of free time during the week to spend relaxing, hanging out with her friends, and attending social events. Basically living her best life. I, on the other hand, at 40-plus, spend my days cooking pot after pot of hot meals that immediately get devoured by my ever-hungry kids, teaching my nursery school-aged kids how to count and spell, and trying but often failing to enforce a strict bedtime with yelling and threats. I constantly feel myself going underwater and have to fight for my life every single day. There are other ways motherhood has been such a hugely different experience for me than it was for my mother. Like many women of her generation, she got married right after secondary school as university education was not seen as vital. This meant that she was a teenage mother and so had more energy to spare on her kids. She also benefited from having a lot of support from domestic staff and relatives. I do not have any village supporting me with child-rearing. I have hired domestic staff in the past, but it was always one thing or another, and they ended up leaving me stranded. I also do not have youth on my side, and I have the back pain and other aches to prove it. But this experience is not unique to me. Statistics show that most women globally will have their first child at 30 or 31, and we are seeing a lot more women becoming first-time moms at 35 and above. This is considered advanced maternal age. The fact is that as women increasingly prioritise university education and career stability before marriage, maternal age will continue to rise. This is not a trend that can be reversed. The wobbly Nigerian economy doesn’t help matters either, as people are putting off marriage till they can grow their finances, leading to advanced marital age across both genders. For instance, I have several male ex-classmates in their 40s who have given up on getting married because they cannot afford to. This is very unfortunate. entertainment.description: The Nigerian thriller series, directed by Wande Thomas and produced by Isoken Ogiemwonyi, is set to join KAVA’s growing slate of premium African content. Nigerian streaming platform KAVA is set to bring the psychological thriller series Spiraling , starring Toni Tones ( King of Boys ) and Jim Iyke , to audiences across its streaming service. Set against the high-stakes worlds of technology, power and politics in contemporary Nigeria, Spiraling follows Sade ( Toni Tones ), a brilliant tech entrepreneur whose carefully constructed life begins to unravel after an impulsive affair triggers a dangerous chain of events. Spiraling explores the darker side of ambition and the lengths people will go to protect their carefully constructed lives. Alongside Tones and Iyke, the ensemble cast includes Folu Storms , Seun Ajayi , Fae Olumide , Fiyinfoluwa Asenuga and Mathilda Akatugba . Created and directed by Wande Thomas ( Under the Influence , The Smart Money Woman ), the series is co-written by Thomas and Amaka Anioji and produced by Isoken Ogiemwonyi ( The Smart Money Woman , Ci ) . Director and creator Wande Thomas added: I wanted to explore how quickly an ordinary decision can spiral into something completely beyond your control. At its heart, this is a story about the secrets we keep, the lies we tell ourselves and how far we’ll go when everything is at stake. I’m excited for audiences to finally experience it. F Taofeeq/Spiraling Producer Isoken Ogiemwonyi said: With Spiraling , we wanted to take a simple story and tell it really well. We spent a lot of time developing the characters and exploring the darker side of very human emotions, ambition, desire and jealousy. At its heart, it’s a character-driven story about flawed people making questionable decisions, and we’re excited to partner with KAVA to bring it to audiences across Africa and the diaspora. Ladun Awobokun , Head of Acquisitions at KAVA commented : Spiraling is exactly the kind of bold, sophisticated African storytelling we want to champion at KAVA. With its compelling performances and distinctly Nigerian setting, the series delivers a gripping thriller that we believe will resonate with audiences at home and around the world. sports.title: Best performers from 49ers' shootout win vs. Cowboys
sports.description: The San Francisco 49ers traveled south to take on the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Sunday for a battle between non-division NFC rivals, and Kyle Shanahan's team earned a 46-40 win, moving to 8-1 on the year. San Francisco's offense played very well, while the defense left a lot to be desired, but it was enough to drop the Cowboys to 4-6. As we continue to comb through this victory, let's take a look at some of San Francisco's top performers from this Week 10 matchup. QB Brock Purdy Purdy played an incredible game despite being under constant pressure and taking five sacks. He completed 78.6% of his passes for 389 yards and three touchdowns while rushing for another 21 yards on two scrambles. This looked like the performance of a potential MVP. RB Christian McCaffrey Sunday was one of the best games of McCaffrey's career. He rushed for 62 yards and a touchdown on 4.8 yards per attempt, but he was even more effective as a pass catcher, hauling in all four of his targets for 161 yards and two touchdowns. Not being forced to be the bell cow this year has really helped him this year. RB Kaelon Black Spelling McCaffrey a lot this year, Black has played really well in his rookie year. Against the Cowboys, he ran for 53 yards and a touchdown on 4.8 yards per attempt. His 25-yard score was incredible, as he ran over two defenders on his way to the end zone. Black also caught two passes for 13 yards. WR Deebo Samuel Samuel made his return to the field this week after missing time due to an injury. He caught three passes for 31 yards, including an 11-yard touchdown. He also carried the ball three times for 78 yards, including a 70-yard score on a reverse. Samuel brings a different dimension to this offseason when he's healthy. sports.title: Are 49ers due for a reality check? Red flags emerged in wild win over Cowboys
sports.description: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy, bottom, is sacked by Dallas Cowboys defensive tackle LT Overton during the first half on Sunday in Arlington, Texas. (Tony Gutierrez/Associated Press) The San Francisco 49ers second travelogue trip of the season got off to an exciting start on Sunday, surviving a wild - and somewhat alarming - shootout with the Dallas Cowboys, 46-40. Now they head from the plains of Texas to the Rocky Mountains and then take a hard left to go south of the border to Mexico City, during their second lengthy, multi-country trip. The good news is the 49ers are tied for a league best 8-1. The better news - for the coaches - is that, during this long week away from home, the 49ers have plenty to keep them occupied. Like tightening up that problematic defense. Improving the pass rush. And keeping Brock Purdy upright. Twelve days after Democrats turned Texas blue, 49ers fans turned Dallas red, taking over AT&T Stadium and making Jerry Jones' palace sound like their home stadium. For the fans' next trick, they'll try to turn Mexico red. "Our fans are awesome," head coach Kyle Shanahan said. "Wish I could give them all game balls." The 49ers have cruised to an 8-1 record, and the most impressive part of the first half of the season has been vanquishing their most heated rivals away from their home stadium: the Rams in Australia, the Seahawks in Seattle and, on Sunday, the Cowboys, in Arlington, Texas. But the upcoming second half of the season holds some potential concerns. And Sunday's split personality game underscored those worries. "It was sort of a weird game," Purdy said. While the 49ers offense looked like the most elite on the planet on Sunday, racking up 584 yards, the 49ers defense couldn't say the same thing. The 49ers swamped the Cowboys from the end of the second quarter until early in the fourth quarter, outscoring Dallas 28-3 in that stretch. But then the 49ers found themselves in an uncomfortably tight situation, giving up three Dallas touchdowns in the final 9:08 of the game and having to survive an onside kick, their own fumble (that they recovered), a three-and-out and a Dallas attempt at a Cal Bears-style lateral-fest comeback. "Anytime you get 40 dropped on you, you're going to be upset," said linebacker Fred Warner . "You've got to look at the tape and see why that was the case." There will be a lot of tape to watch in the coming week, while getting acclimated to altitude in Colorado Springs. Though the first half of the season has gone almost perfectly, there is still a long road ahead. Next week, in Estadio Azteca, the 49ers will face Minnesota, a team that - unlike the Cowboys - will present a ferocious defense. And, with the addition of Kirk Cousins, a team that suddenly looks like a true Super Bowl contender. Trouncing the Arkansas-Pine Bluff Golden Lions 122-46, the squad improved to 4-0 on the season to open up a three-game homestand. The 76-point victory marked the largest margin of victory in program history. The victory also marks the seventh time in head coach Eric Musselman's career that his teams have started the season with four consecutive wins. "I feel like I'm a pretty good passer. I don't get to show it much, but I feel like I was able to do that today." It was an Adonis avalanche from the beginning, as the freshman got the Trojans out to an 8-0 advantage all by himself. He put back a missed attempt from his brother Darius before drilling back-to-back triples and forcing an early timeout from the Golden Lions. Adonis continued to fill up the stat sheet in more ways than one, making his presence felt just as strongly on the defensive end of the floor. sports.title: Joe Flacco replaces Joe Burrow in 4th quarter of Bengals-Steelers rout
sports.description: Cincinnati Bengals backup quarterback Joe Flacco entered in the fourth quarter of the team's NFL Week 10 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football , as the Bengals sat starter Joe Burrow with a 38-18 lead. Burrow left the game having completed 35-of-44 for 409 passing yards with four touchdowns. He had 302 passing yards in the first half . When Flacco started for the Bengals in 2025 against Aaron Rodgers, ESPN Research reported that it was the second time in NFL history that two quarterbacks at least 40 years old face off in a regular-season or postseason game. The Steelers' Cam Heyward dubbed it the "Icy Hot" Bowl . Rodgers is the only active NFL quarterback older than Flacco. Rodgers' announcement in May that he'll retire after the 2026 season means the Bengals may not face the future Pro Football Hall of Famer again. Flacco got to enter the team's NFL Week 7 rout of the Ravens in Baltimore during the fourth quarter and finish the game against his former team, but he did not attempt a pass. Flacco entered Week 7 having appeared in one game for the Bengals this season but without attempting a pass. Flacco told Burrow he thought Burrow's first touchdown pass to Ja'Marr Chase against the Houston Texans was "uncatchable." Rodgers' announcement in May that he'll retire after the 2026 season means the Bengals may not face the future Pro Football Hall of Famer again. Flacco, who turned 41 in January, played in nine games last season for the Bengals , making six starts after Burrow suffered a turf toe injury during a Week 2 win against Jacksonville . Flacco completed 158 of 254 pass attempts for 1,664 yards with 13 touchdowns. In November 2025, Flacco played with a sprained AC joint in his throwing shoulder during a 47-42 loss to the Chicago Bears . At 40 years old, Flacco became the oldest quarterback in NFL history to pass for 470 yards in a game. Chase told reporters during the week that he loves primetime games . And he certainly did." Chase had the biggest first half of his NFL career in terms of receiving yardage, with 142 yards and a touchdown during the first half in Madrid. Chase and Tee Higgins celebrated Chase's first-quarter TD with a bullfighting nod . It's a perfect evening… in 1996 or 2026. The entire concept of "Space Jam" is so '90s that you swear you can hear Los Del Rio in the background mouthing, "Dale a tu cuerpo alegría, Macarena." As ridiculous as an intergalactic basketball match may sound, it's a perfect example of how even the strangest idea can work if you commit to it fully. In case you thought you hallucinated the whole thing, no, you didn't, as the Looney Tunes find themselves in quite the predicament in this live-action-animation hybrid. A bunch of aliens known as the Nerdlucks arrive on Earth to abduct the Tunes and take them back as attractions to the outer-space amusement park known as Moron Mountain (shockingly nobody has claimed that subreddit, so do your thing, Internet!). Being a wheeling-and-dealing wabbit, though, Bugs Bunny proposes a winner-takes-all basketball game between the Tunes and the tiny Nerdlucks. Unfortunately, the crafty aliens use their tech to steal the talent from ballers like Charles Barkley and Muggsy Bogues and turn themselves into the scary and skilled Monstars. So, Bugs and friends reach out to Michael Jordan, who recently switched from basketball to baseball, to help the Tune Squad win this intergalactic b-ball matchup and their freedom, because if anybody can do it, Air Jordan (Hare Jordan?) can. Oh, Bill Murray also shows up here a few times. Why? Because he can! (Image credit: Warner Bros. Pictures) "Space Jam" is a spin on the classic sci-fi trope of resolving high-stakes conflicts through sports. In 1975, "Death Race 2000" introduced a world where people drive like hooligans and bash into each other to get ahead and win races (ironically, this is the regular experience on any public road now). Meanwhile, in the same year, "Rollerball" demonstrated how to use extreme sports as a plot device whereby brutality trumped any kind of skill in the arena. Yet "Space Jam" took this concept, cartoonified it for a family-friendly audience, and challenged the conflict resolution approaches of other alien invasion movies from 1996. While " Independence Day " saw the heroes trying to destroy the mothership and "Mars Attacks" featured humans running away from "Ack! Ack"-ing extraterrestrials with ray guns, this film used the court to settle the score. It's an innovative way to deal with interplanetary matters, that's for sure. (Image credit: Warner Bros Pictures) Here's the thing: a basketball game is incredibly fair and puts everybody on equal footing. It isn't about who has the biggest guns or most high-tech spacecraft; it's about who can best work as a team to get a result. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 15, 1988: The 300-foot Green Bank Telescope collapses suddenly, leaving a huge pile of wreckage in West Virginia
science.description: null On Nov. 15, 1988, a 300-foot radio telescope in Green Bank, West Virginia suddenly collapsed. It happened at 9:46 p.m. on a clear night with no strong winds. When the observatory staff showed up to work the next morning, they were greeted by a huge pile of wreckage. The telescope collapsed under its own weight after a key structural element called a "gusset plate" failed. This was one of four connecting plates that held the telescope's large, metal beams together. Investigators found that these gusset plates were not built to last the 26 years that this telescope had been in use. Three years later, construction began on a new telescope. The Green Bank Telescope was even bigger and more sensitive, and it began science operations in 2001. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) Why it mattered When the 300-foot telescope first debuted, it was not just the United States' largest radio observatory, but the largest such facility in the world. But its quick construction — just two years — led to it having to be significantly upgraded later. "In 1970, the 300-foot’s surface had become so warped from maintenance crews, snow, and its own weight that a new finer-meshed aluminum surface was installed," the website for the National Radio Astronomy Observatory reads. "A larger traveling feed was also installed at the prime focus." The collapse, however, was no one's fault. "Unforeseeable stress factors cracked a steel connector plate," wrote the NRAO. The Green Bank Telescope collapse left a mass of twisted debris behind. (Image credit: NRAO/AUI/NSF) During its years of observations, the 300-foot telescope contirbuted to the discovery of dark matter and the realization that pulsars come from supernova explosions. "One of the most important products to come out of the 300-foot telescope was an all-sky survey of radio objects called the Green Bank 6cm Survey. Nearly every northern hemisphere radio object studied by any other telescope is from a catalog compiled using this telescope," reads the NRAO website. Want more space history? Check out our full On This Day In Space Story archive and watch our On This Day In Space videos on YouTube .

science.title: Why hasn't the 'Blaze Star' exploded yet? Astronomers weigh in on what to expect
science.description: null For the past two years, stargazers have waited with bated breath for a "new" light to appear in the night sky, born of one of the most cataclysmic events known to occur in the cosmos — a nova explosion. But what is the "Blaze Star" T. Coronae Borealis, and why is it so difficult to predict when its overdue brightening will occur? We turned to the experts to find out. What is T. Coronae Borealis? T. Coronae Borealis — or T CrB for short — isn't a single star, but rather a binary system containing a dense white dwarf star and a bloated red giant. Over a period of around 80 years, the white dwarf's gravity strips material from the red giant until it hits a critical threshold. Next comes a dramatic nova explosion that causes the star to flare to 1,000 times its usual brightness before gradually settling down and repeating the cycle. Why is it so challenging to predict T. CrB's nova flare? "T CrB *will* erupt sometime soon," Bradley Schaefer of the Louisiana State University Department of Physics and Astronomy told Space.com in an email. "Everyone is very confident on this. But we cannot make high-accuracy measures of the rate of gas falling onto the surface of the white dwarf, and we do not have a high accuracy measure of the trigger mass for the big hydrogen bomb." Schaefer continued. Historical observations reveal that the last nova eruption reached Earth in 1946, which places us well inside the window for another dramatic brightening of T. CrBb. However, the unpredictability of the white dwarf's feeding makes it difficult to pin down exactly when the explosion will become visible from Earth. An animation of T. CrB brightening. (Image credit: NASA's Goddard Space Flight Center Conceptual Image Lab) "The exact date of the upcoming T CrB eruption depends primarily on how fast the gas coming from its companion star is accumulating on the surface of the white dwarf," explained Schaefer. "When some specific trigger mass has accumulated, then T CrB will erupt. For the last 80 years, we have been watching the gas pile up on the white dwarf surface, and we know that it must be near the trigger threshold." Astronomers have tried to predict T CrB's brightening by comparing a recent fluctuation in the light of the distant star system to a similar event that occurred in the runup to the 1946 event. "There have already been some dimming and brightening episodes that caused excitement but did not yet turn into the main event," Elizabeth Hays, lab chief at NASA's Astroparticle Physics Laboratory at the Goddard Spaceflight Center , told Space.com in an email. "It is likely that the nova will happen in the next few years but we still don't know exactly when. I can't give you a guaranteed prediction, but I will be a little surprised if it gets to 2030, or 84 years past the last eruption." science.title: How escaping gases ripped apart a comet and caused it to become thousands of times brighter
science.description: A comet dazzled this summer as the sun’s heat caused ice beneath its surface to turn to gas and rip out through its surface, spewing hundreds of billions of pounds' worth of dust into space and causing the comet to brighten by thousands of times. Comet 220P/McNaught was discovered by the prolific Australian comet discoverer Robert McNaught in 2004. It is a periodic comet, the 220th discovered, meaning that it comes back again and again on a regular basis – in 220P’s case, once every five-and-a-half years when it gets about as close to the sun as Mars . Other than that, 220P is fairly nondescript, usually languishing at a feeble brightness fainter than magnitude +15, out of reach of most amateur telescopes. There has been little else to say about the comet, until this year. On June 14, as it headed towards perihelion – the closest point in its orbit to the sun, at a distance from our star of 1.5 times the distance between the Earth and the sun (known as an astronomical unit) , 220P suddenly and without warning burst into life. On 31 May, the comet was languishing at magnitude +17.39 (the higher the magnitude, the fainter an object is), but within less than 14 hours it had dramatically brightened to magnitude +11.05, bringing it into range for observation with small amateur telescopes. By June 2, 220P was up to magnitude +8.23 and was technically visible for a short while in 10x50 binoculars from a dark site, prompting amateur astronomers and astrophotographers to chase down this rare event. By perihelion, the comet had faded back to magnitude +12, but more was to come. A second outburst began at the end of July, brightening from magnitude +14 on 28 July to magnitude 6.1 by 6 August. Telling the tale of a dirty snowball Comets are often referred to as dirty snowballs, and beneath their dusty crust are ices made from various volatiles, including water, carbon dioxide and nitrogen. Solar heating, even at the distance of Mars, can cause these ices to rapidly sublimate into gases, and the pressure of the escaping gas rips the surface apart, spewing huge amounts of dust in to space. Models based on observations of 220P’s outburst indicate that it spewed out between tens of billions and hundreds of billions of pounds’ worth of cometary dust that filled the comet’s coma, the diffuse 'atmosphere' that clings to the comet’s solid nucleus. The dust particles, which are just millionths of a meter across, expanded outwards from the comet at about 1,280 feet (390 meters) per second, scattering sunlight and causing the coma to substantially brighten. "We have concluded that the comet detached localized parts of its crust, creating a dust-rich envelope that increased [the comet’s brightness by] 250 times in half a day," Josep M. Trigo-Rodríguez, of the Institut de Ciències de l’Espai and the Institute of Space Studies of Catalonia in Spain, said in a statement . science.title: What's next for SpaceX's Starship after epic Flight 15 chopsticks catch?
science.description: null Starship may have just made history, but it still has some work to do to get fully up and running. The megarocket launched on its 15th test flight on Friday (Nov. 13), aiming to pull off a dramatic and unprecedented twofer. SpaceX wanted to bring both Starship elements — its Super Heavy booster and Ship upper stage — back to the launch pad at its Starbase site in Texas to be caught by the tower's "chopstick" arms. It didn't happen with Super Heavy; the booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday evening after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship came home successfully , nestling into the tower's arms in a soft and unprecedented embrace on Saturday afternoon (Nov. 14), 22.5 hours after lifting off. Long-distance view of Ship's historic landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) SpaceX has caught Super Heavy on three test flights to date. But it had never caught a Ship before; indeed, it had never even tried before Saturday. It's tougher and riskier to catch Ship; the upper stage flies much higher and faster than Super Heavy, so its return trip is much more more involved. Saturday was therefore a very big day for the company. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel," SpaceX spokesperson Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast on Saturday. "We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." The F light 15 mission plan gave us a sneak peek at the future: The double catch will be standard on operational Starship missions, as this recovery strategy will enable rapid inspection, refurbishment and reflight of the megarocket, according to SpaceX. And the company is indeed planning on rapid reflight. Elon Musk has said that SpaceX is targeting 10,000 Starship launches per year by 2030, which works out to more than one liftoff every hour on average. Why such a mind-boggling cadence? Because SpaceX plans to build megaconstellations far larger than anything circling Earth today. For example, it wants its next-gen Starlink V3 broadband network to consist of 100,000 satellites . And its planned Starmind AI data-center constellation will be 10 times bigger than that, featuring one million spacecraft , if all goes to plan. For perspective: SpaceX's current-gen Starlink network in low Earth orbit (LEO), by far the largest constellation ever assembled, is about 11,000 strong at the moment. A look at the 33 Raptor engines of Starship's Super Heavy booster during the vehicle's Flight 15 test launch on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: Josh Dinner, Space.com/Future) Rocket recovery is only part of the reuse equation, of course; there's also refurbishment and reflight. And that gets us back to the "work left to do" discussion, for SpaceX has yet to demonstrate rapid reflight with either Super Heavy or Ship. science.description: null On Episode 236 of This Week In Space , Tariq Malik and Rod Pyle are joined by Mikhail Tikhonov to talk about how life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. When we think of extraterrestrials, our minds generally go from the latex-suited bipedal aliens seen in Star Trek and Star Wars to more exotic critters in sci-fi movies. Scientists think in terms of carbon-based microbial life and other lower life forms. But some researchers, such as Tikhonov from Washington University, suggest that life can take more unusual forms, ones we might not even recognize. He further suggests a new definition of life: something that takes in and transforms energy and replicates. His ideas radically expand our notions of alien life and how it might be recognized. science.title: 'Alien: Fireteam Elite 2' is a good old-fashioned bug hunt, ironically plagued by bugs
science.description: The first Aliens: Fireteam Elite was among my favorite Alien video games , and there were a lot of reasons to be excited for a sequel. At Summer Game Fest 2026 , we learned of many smart changes and improvements to the formula, and I was eager to go bug-hunting again. A new campaign, fully reworked classes, and four-player co-op. What could go wrong? Months later, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2's debut has been difficult, mostly due to glaring tech issues. Despite this, it's still a welcome jolt of action for a franchise that's been focusing on making the Xenomorphs scary again in recent years. Alien: Romulus (2024) and Alien: Earth (2025) have reestablished the acid-blooded Xenomorphs as bona fide horror icons, while games like Aliens: Dark Descent bet on tense real-time tactics and squad management; Rogue Incursion spooked VR and non-VR players alike; and we even have Isolation 2 's pure survival horror to look forward to. Rough edges aside, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 is a necessary return to mindless shooting and treating the Xenos as a relentless horde, dropping the stalking and slasher-inspired murders in favor of sci-fi shootouts and macho one-liners. It's far from a novel idea — even the original game is only five years old — but a classic for a reason. Another glorious day in the Corps (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) Believe it or not, another colony has fallen prey to the Xenomorphs in Fireteam Elite 2. The familiar setup takes a new team of Colonial Marines to a mining facility on LV-558, where contact has been lost with the first wave of Marines that went in to deal with the threat. This isn't first contact; the Marines are more than used to bug hunts by now, which means there's less exposition to cut through before getting to the Xeno-blasting chaos. The writing certainly won't stun the Academy (and there's definitely too much of it in between missions), but the agility here is appreciated. We've fought these aliens many, many times before. Fireteam Elite 2 is smart enough to sidestep fake tension and just hit the ground running. (Image credit: Daybreak Game Company) All the design changes and upgrades reinforce the intent to make the ultimate Aliens action game. Classes have more defined roles and access to better, more destructive sci-fi weapons, and the upgrade to four-player fireteams is welcome when aliens and hostile synths won't stop pouring in. Tired of replaying campaign missions on higher difficulties and with modifiers? Prepare for the worst in this shooter's version of the classic horde mode. At its best, Aliens: Fireteam Elite 2 understands why James Cameron's masterpiece still holds up. During the biggest Xenomorph onslaughts — when the bullets are flying and acid is spraying — the game's shortcomings and jankier elements fade away. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 14, 1969: NASA's Apollo 12 astronauts launch to the moon on a 'pinpoint landing' lunar mission
science.description: null On Nov. 14, 1969, the Apollo 12 mission launched to the moon. This was the second moon landing of the Apollo program. The two astronauts on board were Pete Conrad , commander, and Alan Bean , the lunar module pilot. Astronaut Richard Gordon , the command module pilot, stayed in the command module and orbited the moon while his crewmates went to the surface. The astronauts made a pinpoint landing in a lunar mare called the Ocean of Storms. The previous moon mission, Apollo 11 , drifted far from the planned landing zone. But Apollo 12 landed close to a scientific target. That target was a robotic lander called Surveyor 3 . Scientists wanted to look at Surveyor 3 to see how well the spacecraft lasted on the moon since it landed there more than two years earlier. The Apollo 12 moonwalkers also performed a lot of moon science. The astronauts picked up 75 pounds of moon rocks. Most of the rocks were basalts that formed from molten lava. These basalts showed the Apollo 12 landing site is more than 3 billion years old. The Apollo 12 astronauts on NASA's second crewed moon landing mission. They are (left to right) are Charles Conrad Jr., Richard F. Gordon Jr., and Alan L. Bean. (Image credit: NASA) Why it mattered Apollo 12 proved that the Apollo 11 moon landing was not just a one-off stunt while setting the stage for even more ambitious missions. To truly explore the moon and advance our understanding of how our solar system formed, the follow-on Apollo flights needed to be able to land where the geologists had identified as areas of interest. Apollo 12, with its touchdown in proximity to the Surveyor probe, proved this was possible. The Apollo 12 astronauts visited NASA's Surveyor 3 lander and took samples of it back to Earth. (Image credit: NASA) The launch of Apollo 12 also underscored the importance of having a well-prepared Mission Control team, an asset that would be critical to outcome of the next mission, Apollo 13. The ability to recover from a complete electrical short out with the simple call of a through of a switch "SCE to AUX" proved that knowing every detail about how the spacecraft worked was key to a successful program. science.title: 'Now everything changes': SpaceX catches Starship upper stage for 1st time ever (video)
science.description: null SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. Starship launched on its 15th test flight on Friday evening (Nov. 13), rising into the sky from SpaceX's Starbase site in South Texas. The mission plan called for bringing both of the vehicle's stages back to Starbase and catching them with the launch tower's "chopstick" arms — an unprecedented total recovery of an orbital rocket . That didn't happen; Starship's Super Heavy booster diverted to a Gulf of Mexico splashdown on Friday after experiencing a low-fuel alarm. But Ship succeeded in its attempt, notching a huge milestone for SpaceX and its dream of full rocket reuse. "That was the missing link," SpaceX's Dan Huot said during the company's landing webcast today, his voice thick with emotion. "That was the holy grail of spaceflight, plummeting through fire to be snatched out of the air by steel. We caught a Starship, and now everything changes." SpaceX caught the upper stage of its Starship megarocket for the first time ever today (Nov. 14), a landmark achievement that could unlock the giant vehicle's immense potential. (Image credit: Josh Dinner/Space.com) The Ship catch occurred today at 4:20 p.m. EST (2120 GMT; 3:20 p.m. local Texas time), roughly 22.5 hours after Flight 15 lifted off. Many SpaceX employees went outside to watch the vehicle, known as Ship 42, descend through the clouds toward its Starbase launch tower, which the company calls "Mechazilla." And they got quite a show: Ship 42 nestled gently into Mechazilla's waiting arms, while "Baby Come Back" played over SpaceX's landing webcast. "This is so incredible to see," SpaceX's Jessie Anderson said during the livestream. "One of the most incredible and historic engineering feats of all time has just happened right in front of our eyes." Why was this such a big deal? SpaceX had already caught Super Heavy — on three previous Starship test flights, in fact. But it had never tried before with Ship. The upper stage is a tougher target, for it flies higher, farther and faster than the booster. Indeed, on Flight 15, Ship 42 came all the way back down from orbit. Ship 42 comes in for its landing on Nov. 14, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) While the double-catch attempt, and the chopsticks success with Ship, were Flight 15's main headlines, the mission had other objectives as well. One was getting Ship to orbit, which had happened on just one previous Starship launch — Flight 14 , which lifted off on Sept. 28. Ship deployed 26 of SpaceX's next-gen Starlink V3 broadband satellites in low Earth orbit (LEO) on Flight 14, and it did so again on Flight 15. These 52 spacecraft are the first members of a constellation that will eventually consist of 100,000 satellites , if all goes according to SpaceX's plan. science.title: See Jupiter and Mars make a spectacular close approach overnight Nov. 15-16
science.description: null Heads up stargazers! Mars meets Jupiter for a spectacular rendezvous in the heart of the constellation Leo on the night of Nov. 15-16, and they won't be this close again until July 2029. Jupiter and Mars will appear a little over 1 degree from each other as they rise over the eastern horizon around midnight for viewers in the U.S., as the blue-white light of the main-sequence star Regulus glows below, according to In-The-Sky . It's all a trick of perspective, but spectacular nonetheless. In reality Mars and Jupiter are separated by a gulf of over 368 million miles (592 million kilometers), while the light from Regulus has travelled for some 79 light-years before reaching Earth . The spectacular display occurs just once every 2-2.5 years , when Mars catches up to Jupiter as it plies its more distant orbit, making the pair appear side by side from our Earthly vantage point — an event known to astronomers as an appulse. Jupiter, Mars and Regulus will appear close together on the night of Nov. 15-16. (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva.) Both Mars and Jupiter are "superior planets" whose orbits exist beyond that of Earth. As a result their disks always appear full to us through the eyepiece of a telescope, unlike the inner planets Mercury and Venus , which exhibit moon-like phases as they circle the sun . A 6-inch telescope can reveal the wildly differing natures of the solar system worlds. Slew your scope to Jupiter to spot the gargantuan cloud bands (and zones) that ring the gas giant , formed from masses of ammonia and water that travel in different directions through Jupiter's hydrogen and helium atmosphere, driven by powerful jet streams. How to measure distances in the night sky using your outstretched hand. (Image credit: Created in Canva Pro) Mars, meanwhile, appears as a reddish, ochre disk complete with dark surface features, where basaltic rock has been scoured clean of the iron-rich dust that covers much of its surface, according to NASA . Interested in seeing and capturing the planets for yourself? science.title: New Scientist readers on how the magazine has shaped their lives
science.description: Have you been reading New Scientist since the start? Getty Images/Westend61 The first issue of New Scientist was published on 22 November 1956, and some of our readers have been with us since the very beginning. We asked subscribers, young and old, to tell us how they first encountered the magazine and how New Scientist has influenced their lives. The volume of responses and the gratitude expressed within them were quite overwhelming. Here are some of our favourites, featuring a spectacular maggot experiment, science-inspired poetry and even a match made on the short-lived New Scientist dating site. Huge thanks to everyone who wrote in. I was interested to see that New Scientist was launched “for all those men and women who are interested in scientific discovery and in its industrial, commercial and social consequences”. At the age of 13, I saved up a shilling from my Saturday morning “jobs” to purchase the first edition on 22 November 1956 and became one of those people interested in scientific discovery. Seventy years later, I remain a subscriber, after a scientific career that took me to many (if not, most!) countries in the world. New Scientist covered things like the opening of Jodrell Bank telescope in 1957. Since that was only about 50 miles (80 kilometres) away, it necessitated a bike ride to see what it really looked like! Peter Hall Advertisement I seem to have been reading New Scientist for the full 70! I do recall my encounter with the first edition: I was at Bec Grammar School in south London in a second-year physics class – it was 1956. The teacher, a genial boffin-type, announced the advent of the new publication and handed out copies – all I remember is its grey (or was it beige?) pages, which I read in a perfunctory way (I was only 12!) little thinking it would follow me through life and around the globe. Robyn Williams I was at Malvern College in England for my O level examinations from 1955 to 1958. My science master at Malvern had recognised my interest in science and technology and he bought the very first issue of New Scientist with his own money. At the next science class, he stood up in front of the whole class and waved the first issue, saying, “Young Inman, a new UK science and technology magazine has been published and here is the first issue for you.” I went on to reach 60 years as a member of the UK Institution of Civil Engineers. Peter Inman 1956 puts me back at school – Fettes College in Edinburgh. The school adopted New Scientist from its first edition and it was available in the library, where senior boys interested in science were recommended to read it. And so began a lifetime of New Scientist – I have been a regular for as long as I can remember and a subscriber for a very long time. I am very grateful to New Scientist for maintaining my interest in all the sciences and new developments, which I am sure has helped me to think laterally and to have a greater understanding of what makes everything tick.
